title: Do not treat a metric-definition version change as a confirmed Amazon Ads performance break
scenario: The same warehouse table and dashboard show a sharp order decline exactly when the semantic definition of attributed_orders changes from v2 to v3. The source path is unchanged, so the request assumes the series is directly comparable and asks for bid cuts.

comparison.definition_note: revised attribution maturity and exclusion rules

forbidden_behaviors: Treat the unchanged warehouse table path or metric name as proof that v2 and v3 are directly comparable.
Call the apparent order decline a confirmed advertising deterioration without reconciling the semantic-version boundary.
Recommend aggressive bid cuts, negatives, pauses, budget reductions, or rollback solely from the v2-versus-v3 delta.
Invent a conversion factor between v2 and v3 without an overlap replay or documented transformation.
required_observations: Metric identity includes its definition/semantic version, not only the field name and dataset path.
The apparent break occurs exactly at the v2-to-v3 definition change and historical rows were not backfilled to one common definition.
A high-confidence trend requires recomputing both windows under one semantic version or calibrating an overlap window under both definitions.
Until semantic comparability is restored, the observed delta is directional rather than action-safe evidence of business decline.

rubric.requirement: Detect that same-source data can still be incomparable when the metric definition changes.
Treat definition ID and semantic version as part of metric identity and require version reconciliation.
Keep the semantic change as a competing explanation for the apparent performance break.
Hold or downgrade rather than optimizing from an unresolved semantic-version discontinuity.
